id: ON&ON Presents Richard Sen (UK) and Christopher Tubbs-Cuba St Tavern, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: ON&ON Presents Richard Sen (UK) and Christopher Tubbs
long_description:
Winter is over and ON&ON is back! On October 31st head honcho Christopher Tubbs will be joined by London's Richard Sen, a legendary DJ, producer, broadcaster and graffiti artist, whose distinctly diverse sound and curatorial skills have earned him international acclaim.

Christopher Tubbs has this to say:

“It’s always been a dream of mine to have my all-time favourite DJ play one of my parties. When I first heard London-based Richard Sen play in Brixton during the summer of ‘97, he totally blew my mind. It was a total epiphany and totally changed the way I thought about my own DJing. I stood side of booth desperately wanting to ask him what every record he played was, but I managed to hold it down using my last dregs of self respect”...

As most regular ON&ON party people know, this daytime get-together sells out in the shake of a lamb's tail, so don't hang about! Join us in that beautiful botanical courtyard at Cuba St Tavern for a day into night of Balearic burners, deep disco, classic house inspiration and post punk detonations.

P.S- we might go a little later than 11pm;)

id: The Bon Temps Bros-Hilltop Private House Concerts, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: The Bon Temps Bros
long_description:
Gate opens 7pm, Music starts 7.30pm.

Pip Payne, Richard Klein and Alan Norman are The Bon Temps Bros. PIP PAYNE, a regular player and founder of Capital Blues is back with another musical variation. Pip has had many artistic guises over the years which shows not only his versatility, bluesy vocals but also his depth of the music. He plays slide guitar, and plays regularly with Wayne Mason, Pops & The Tempests, the Caramellos, Dean Martinborough, Laura Collins Back Porch Band and more. Originally from Dorking, he now lives in Otaki Beach. RICHARD KLEIN is a high energy singing fiddler born in Orange, New Jersey. In his early teens he discovered folk and roots music through listening to the likes of Woody Guthrie, Pete Seeger and The New Lost City Ramblers. Travelling to Cape Breton Island in mid 1970s sparked the interest for Celtic music that later brought Richard to travel, live, work and busk extensively through Ireland and the British Isles. A chance meeting with a gang of Swedish fiddlers in Shetland in 1978 introduced another important influence in his fiddle style. But it was being properly introduced to Cajun music later that same year in France that had the most profound impact on his music. Resident in Wellington since 1997, Richard is best known for his collaboration with the Le Blanc Brothers Cajun Band (Melbourne) and the geographically challenged Kiwi Americana band. T-Bone. In 2023 he relinquished his American citizenship. The accent, however, remains and you will find him to be a charming gentleman. AL NORMAN has been on the Wellington scene for decades. A multi-instrumentalist with a great feel for the groove, he plays with The Warratahs, Rag Poets, Bill Lake’s Slow Bake and Burgin, Kerr & Norman. He’s been part of a number of well-established groups including Smokeshop and The Laura Collins Band.

… A slide guitar, a fiddle, an accordion, and a snare drum. Together they make a big sound – and it’s all about the groove. Acoustically syncopated Cajun blues — hot Louisiana music.

Come along and enjoy this great gig in our special space, up close and personal.
These are private house concerts, not for profit, supporting our dedicated musicians. Visit www.hilltophouseconcerts.co.nz to reserve a seat. Suggested donation $30. Email confirmation will include address and details. Teas, Coffee and Snacks provided. You're welcome to bring anything you'd like to eat or drink. Parking available in the Coupon zones of Upland Rd & Glasgow St free after 6pm weekdays, and free all through the weekends. The Wilson Carpark at the top of the Cable Car charges 24/7.

id: Anthonie Tonnon Presents Cinematographer-Hannah Playhouse, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Anthonie Tonnon Presents Cinematographer
long_description:
Taite Music Prize-winning songwriter Anthonie Tonnon presents his immersive new live show, Cinematographer.

Three years in the making, Cinematographer combines live electronic music, cinematic storytelling and visual design into an immersive performance. Featuring visual DJing by Erica Sklenars, videography by Theo Taylor, styling by Karlya Smith and design by Daniel Alexander, the show sees Tonnon playing the roles of DJ, singer, documentarian and revolutionary lecturer.

The show explores two timelines: the Situationist International in France and Italy during the 1960s, and Whanganui, New Zealand at the turn of the millennium - a mysterious, forgotten city where a new battle is being waged against what Guy Debord famously called The Society of the Spectacle.

Swapping his guitar for a vocoder, and transforming two Synthstrom Deluges into honorary turntables, Tonnon connects these seemingly distant worlds through the musical language of turn-of-the-millennium dance culture.

Cinematographer is part film, part francophile performance lecture, part disco club set, says Tonnon. It's a world that we've built for this new music, exploring some newfound passions – the French avant-garde, cinema, urban politics of the 1960s, turn-of-the-millennium dance culture and documentary films, and the glorious, mystifying city of Whanganui.

The ambitious audiovisual performance introduces an entirely new body of work developed with Tonnon's band and longtime producer Jonathan Pearce. The new single and video Executive Assistant offers the first glimpse into this new world - Tonnon's first new music in three years.

Doors open: 8.45PM I Show 9:15PM

Unallocated seating and standing available.

Early Bird tickets available until Monday 10 August or until allocation sells out.

id: Songwriters' Saturday-The Realm Bar & Bistro, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Songwriters' Saturday
long_description:
Welcome to the October Songwriters' Saturday at https://therealm.co.nz/

We have another exciting evening of homegrown music planned for your enjoyment. Things kick off at 6.30 p.m. with the first of three acts. Your host venue, The Realm, is fully seated, with Bar and Restaurant facilities available and is close to bus services. Reservations can be made online or by phone. Parking is free and, on the street, with easy access from the front of the building. The music ends around 9 o'clock.

About the Artists:

Goldenchild: Our unlikely crew is as follows; - Matt on Bass, Chuck - Drums and Mo on Vocals and guitar. We are proud to share our music with you. Goldenchild is surprising and unexpected. Rich songwriting to make you feel intensely, and to dance, and sing. Lush acoustic rhythms, dense funk grooves, and the catchiest melodies.

Glenn Barclay: Glenn has been writing (and playing) the occasional song for many years and now it appears that they all add up to something that he would like to share with everyone. Glenn, and his guitar, will be joined by Eric Daubé on backing vocals.

Jane Shearer: Jane loves telling stories through music, with humour. Her performances use guitar or cello, whichever tells the story best. Jane's recent album Menagerie exemplifies her indie-quirk approach to songwriting.

Rachel Hird: Rachel is a Wellington based singer-songwriter. She grew up playing the piano and studying classical music. Nowadays she is living the dream, writing and performing her own songs and connecting with people in the music community. She is constantly inspired by people, places and events of the past and present and has recently released a debut EP - ‘Through the Page’.
